topicName: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) & AWX
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Enterprise Automation with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform and AWX"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) is the enterprise-grade framework for scaling IT automation. AWX is the upstream open-source project that serves as the upstream for AAP, providing a web-based user interface, REST API, and task engine built on top of Ansible. In this tutorial, you will learn how to configure an automation controller project, manage inventories, and execute jobs programmatically."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Architecture"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A running instance of AWX or Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"An execution environment containing your required collections and Python dependencies."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic familiarity with Ansible playbooks and YAML syntax."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Structuring Your Project Repository"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"AWX and AAP require your playbooks and roles to be structured within a Version Control System (VCS) like Git. A standard project repository includes a playbooks directory, roles, and a collection requirements file."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"repo-root/
├── collections/
│   └── requirements.yml
├── playbooks/
│   └── site.yml
└── roles/
    └── webserver/
        ├── tasks/
        │   └── main.yml
        └── vars/
            └── main.yml"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Defining Collection Requirements"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"When using custom execution environments, you must declare any required Ansible collections in the collections/requirements.yml file so the controller can automatically install them during project synchronization."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"---
collections:
  - name: amazon.aws
    version: ">=5.0.0"
  - name: ansible.posix
    version: ">=1.4.0""},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Writing an Enterprise Playbook"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create an enterprise-ready playbook inside your playbooks/site.yml directory. This playbook applies the webserver role to target nodes defined dynamically in your controller inventory."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"---
- name: Configure Web Servers
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  gather_facts: true
  roles:
    - webserver"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Interacting via the AWX/AAP REST API"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Beyond the web user interface, AAP and AWX provide a robust REST API. You can trigger job templates programmatically using curl or any HTTP client by passing your organization credentials."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"curl -X POST https://your-aap-controller.example.com/api/v2/job_templates/42/launch/ \
  -u "username:password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"extra_vars": {"deployment_version": "v1.2.0"}}'"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully learned how to structure an automation project for Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform and AWX, manage collection dependencies, write modular playbooks, and launch jobs via the API. Scale these concepts across your enterprise for secure, repeatable IT operations."}]
